subject: Jurisdictional data handling - appendix language and retention carveouts
messages:
From: Delphic Health Legal <legal@delphichealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Delphic Health CloudOps <ops@delphichealth.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: DPA redlines - residency & deletion appendix

Neha —

Thanks for sending through the draft DPA. Our legal team redlined a couple of areas where we need clearer commitments on jurisdictional handling and proof of deletion. High-level asks:

- Can Redwood commit to the proposed "territory locking" language that prevents cross-border restore of live customer data without prior consent?
- We need an enforceable retention schedule for production + backup copies and an evidence path for erasure requests (on-demand erasure + backup deletion).
- For backups, we need a maximum retention of 90 days unless otherwise agreed and a certification process for deletion (audit log + certificate or third-party validation).

Attached is our marked-up DPA (Delphic_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf). Our CloudOps team is copied on technical follow-ups.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide an appendix describing the erasure evidence workflow (what artifacts you provide, timing, and runbook)?

Thanks,
Erin MacLeod
Senior Counsel, Delphic Health
legal@delphichealth.com

Subject: Re: DPA redlines - residency & deletion appendix

Erin —

Appreciate the detailed review and the attached redlines. We want to be practical and certifiable here — happy to put an appendix in the DPA describing the erasure evidence workflow and to narrow the residency language so it meets Delphic's controls. A few quick notes up front:

- Territory locking: we can commit to not restoring live production customer data outside the contractually-specified region except for explicit written consent or legal process. We will add a clause that any cross-border restore for operational purposes requires a documented approval chain (customer POA + Redwood signoff) and a timestamped audit trail.

- Backups: Redwood uses tiered backups. For production backups we propose a 90-day retention default with the option for customers to select shorter windows. For snapshot backups used for troubleshooting we can support a 30-day maximum unless otherwise agreed in writing.

- Evidence of deletion: we can include an erasure appendix describing the artifacts we provide upon completion:
  * deletion confirmation with UTC timestamp
  * storage object identifiers that were deleted (where applicable)
  * system audit logs showing erase operations and operator IDs
  * KMS key-rotation / decryption-denial timestamp (if BYOK used)

We also attach our internal playbook (redwood-erase-playbook-2028.pdf) that maps steps to artifacts.

I'll align with Marcus and Jonas on tightening the proposed clause text and send a counter-draft by EOD Monday. If there's a specific compliance form you want us to fill out (e.g., SOC / ISO evidence checklist), point me to it and we'll coordinate with our compliance team.

Best,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Sep 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed DPA appendix language

Neha / Jonas —

Draft language below that I tested with infra: please sanity-check for legal tone. I tried to balance Delphic's ask for evidence with operational realities (snapshots, immutable backups, provider-side retention windows).

--- PROPOSED APPENDIX LANGUAGE (for insertion into DPA) ---

1. Territory Locking
Redwood shall not restore or transfer Customer Production Data to a physical location outside the contractually specified geographic region (the "Territory") without prior written consent of the Customer, except where required by applicable law. Any such restore shall be recorded in Redwood's audit logs including time, operator identity, justification, and Customer approval reference.

2. Backup Retention
Redwood shall maintain production backups for a default retention period of up to ninety (90) days. Customers may elect a shorter retention period at provisioning. For transient debugging snapshots, Redwood may retain copies for up to thirty (30) days unless Customer requests earlier deletion in writing.

3. Erasure Evidence and Certification
Upon Customer's verified request for deletion, Redwood will:
  a. Initiate deletion of Customer data from live systems within forty-eight (48) hours of request receipt;
  b. Initiate deletion of backups in accordance with the Customer's retention settings and within a maximum of ninety (90) days for production backups unless Customer requests an expedited deletion (paid rapid-erase option available);
  c. Provide a deletion certificate within seven (7) business days that includes: UTC timestamp(s) of deletion operations, storage object identifiers (where available), audit log excerpts showing the deletion operation and operator IDs, and a statement of scope (systems and backups included).

4. Evidence Limitations
Redwood will provide all artifacts available within its operational environment. For third-party storage or archival solutions where Redwood does not have direct deletion control, Redwood will provide the vendor's deletion confirmation and any available vendor audit artifacts.

--- end language ---

Notes:
- Infra confirms we can produce the described artifacts; the rapid-erase paid option covers expedited manual workflows for backups outside the normal cycle.
- We should include an explicit reference to BYOK behavior (if Delphic uses BYOK, key destruction denies access and acts as logical erase).

If that language looks good, Neha, can you send to Erin with Redlines tracked?

Thanks,
Marcus
Principal PM, Platform Reliability
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Erin MacLeod <legal@delphichealth.com>
Cc: Delphic Health CloudOps <ops@delphichealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Sep 2028 16:48:00 -0400
Subject: RE: DPA redlines - residency & deletion appendix

Erin —

Thanks again for the markups. We've reviewed and propose the attached appendix text as a counter-proposal. High level summary of changes vs your redlines:

- We accept a strict territory-locking commitment for restores of live production data and will add the audit-trail requirement. This does not apply to telemetry or aggregated non-PII metrics used for platform health.
- For backups, we propose the default 90-day production retention with a customer-selectable shorter window; we also offer a paid rapid-erase option for expedited backup deletion within 7 business days (captures the operational cost of manual reconciliation).
- For erasure evidence, we will provide a deletion certificate within 7 business days containing the artifacts outlined below. Where Redwood relies on a third-party vendor for storage or long-term archival beyond Redwood's operational control, Redwood will provide the vendor confirmation and vendor-provided artifacts.

Artifacts we will deliver with each deletion certificate:
- UTC timestamp(s) of erase steps and confirmation(s)
- Storage object identifiers or blob keys (when applicable)
- Audit log excerpt(s) showing erase operation, operator ID, and job run id
- Reference to any KMS key operations relevant to the erasure (if BYOK in use)

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether the 7-business-day deletion certificate timeline is acceptable to Delphic or if you require a faster SLA (we can push to 3 business days using the rapid-erase add-on).
2) If acceptable, we'll prepare a tracked-changes DPA appendix and a short one-page playbook for your CloudOps to review (includes runbook steps, expected artifacts, and troubleshooting checklist).

If you'd like a quick sync to walk through the artifacts and the rapid-erase flow, Marcus and Jonas are available tomorrow morning PST.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & GRC, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
